arabic_text: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
english_text: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
reflection_note: This verse is a reminder that your capacity is known to Allah, even when you feel stretched beyond words.

arabic_text: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ۝ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
english_text: So surely with hardship comes ease. Surely with that hardship comes more ease.
reflection_note: The promise of ease is repeated, giving the heart permission to keep going through a difficult season.

english_text: Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort.
reflection_note: When the heart feels unsettled, remembrance can become a steady place to return to.

english_text: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.
reflection_note: A guilty heart is not asked to run from Allah; it is invited back to His mercy.

arabic_text: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ ۝ وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ ۝ وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ
english_text: Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He become hateful of you. And the next life is certainly far better for you than this one. And your Lord will give you, and you will be pleased.
reflection_note: These verses meet loneliness with reassurance that Allah's care has not left you.

english_text: If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more.
reflection_note: Joy can become worship when it turns into gratitude.

english_text: Do not falter or grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers.
reflection_note: This verse speaks to moments when sadness begins to feel like defeat.

arabic_text: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
english_text: Whoever puts their trust in Allah, then He alone is sufficient for them.
reflection_note: Tawakkul does not erase effort; it places the outcome with the One who knows the unseen.

arabic_text: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلَا وَصَبٍ وَلَا هَمٍّ وَلَا حَزَنٍ وَلَا أَذًى وَلَا غَمٍّ إِلَّا كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
english_text: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm, or distress touches a Muslim except that Allah expiates some sins through it.
reflection_note: Pain is not meaningless before Allah; even unseen heaviness can carry spiritual reward.

arabic_text: عَجَبًا لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ
english_text: The believer's affair is amazing: if good comes, they are grateful; if hardship comes, they are patient, and both are good for them.
reflection_note: This hadith frames both ease and difficulty as paths back to Allah.

english_text: Allah says that He is as His servant thinks of Him, and He is with the servant when they remember Him.
reflection_note: Hold a hopeful opinion of Allah; remembrance is a way of realizing His nearness.

english_text: Tie it, and then put your trust in Allah.
reflection_note: Trust in Allah sits beside responsible action, not in place of it.

arabic_text: وَمَا اجْتَمَعَ قَوْمٌ فِي بَيْتٍ مِنْ بُيُوتِ اللَّهِ يَتْلُونَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَيَتَدَارَسُونَهُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِلَّا نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّكِينَةُ
english_text: When people gather to recite and study the Book of Allah, tranquility descends upon them, mercy covers them, and angels surround them.
reflection_note: If loneliness is heavy, the Quran and good company can both become means of sakinah.

english_text: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a person who finds their lost mount in the wilderness.
reflection_note: Repentance is not a humiliation before Allah; it is a return that He loves.

english_text: True patience is at the first shock of calamity.
reflection_note: The first wave of pain is hard; this hadith honors the struggle to respond with patience in that moment.

english_text: After being rejected and harmed at Ta'if, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ turned to Allah in deep need and did not answer cruelty with revenge.
reflection_note: Rejection can be carried with dignity; being hurt does not mean being abandoned by Allah.
reference: Seerah: Journey to Ta'if, reported in Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq traditions and hadith accounts

english_text: During the Hijrah, when Abu Bakr feared discovery in the cave, the Prophet ﷺ reassured him that Allah was with them.
reflection_note: Fear can exist beside faith; reassurance often begins with remembering Allah's nearness.
reference: Seerah: Hijrah and Cave of Thawr; see Quran 9:40

english_text: When revelation first came and the Prophet ﷺ was shaken, Khadijah رضي الله عنها comforted him by naming his goodness and service to others.
reflection_note: In moments of fear, it is a mercy to lean on trusted people who remind you of what is true.

english_text: After the painful setback at Uhud, the Muslim community was taught to reflect, repent, and remain steady rather than collapse into despair.
reflection_note: A setback can become a turning point when it leads to humility, learning, and renewed trust in Allah.
reference: Seerah: Battle of Uhud; see Quran 3:139-142
